request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's crew total, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**The change (front end only):**
- **Header** (`features/header/header.ts`): a new "My crews' due" figure, `my-crew-due-total`, next to "My due" and "My overdue".
- **How it's worked out** (`features/people/people.ts`): it finds the user's person the same way "My due" already does, by name or alias with case ignored. It then adds up the due-totals of every crew that person leads. If there's no such person, or they lead no crew, it's blank.
- **Crews** (`features/crews/crews.ts`): the crews list is now shared with the people page, so the header can read it. I moved the per-crew due-total sum into a shared `crewDueCents()` function. The crew rows and the header both use it, so they always give the same figure.

**Two server bugs fixed along the way.** Two of the four scenarios also failed when I backed my change out, so these bugs were already there. Both are in `claim/ClaimService.java`:
1. **Bulk settle crashed** when a selected claim's due was n/a (no rate for its grade), because it tried to add a missing value into the batch total. It now skips n/a dues, which gives the `total=0.00` the test expects.
2. **The claim log showed the wrong due on a new claim** when a rate only applies to claims added after it was set. The log line was written before the claim was saved, so it didn't yet know when it was added and used the older rate (1.25 instead of 1.00). In both adding a claim and splitting one, it's now logged right after the first save.
